title: Do Claude workers pick up the [workers] model and effort before the worker code switches to Workers::resolved?
body:
**Chose:** `config::load` writes the Claude-fallback resolution into each role's concrete `Worker.model`/`Worker.effort` when the role keeps Claude and does not set the key itself, and `knobs` reports such an inherited value as `user`. `WorkerSources` still records only keys set in the role's own table, so `Workers::resolved` can tell them apart.
**Over:** Leaving the concrete fields at `opus`/`high` until a later slice moves `worker.rs` to `Workers::resolved`.
**Because:** Without this, a top-level `[workers] model = "sonnet"` (which `factory setup` will write) would parse but do nothing for today's Claude-only workers, and the run's knobs row would say `default`. This slice may not touch `worker.rs`.
**Undo:** Remove `inherit_worker_defaults` and the `inherited` branch in `knobs` (src/config.rs).

title: What review effort applies when [review] effort is unset?
body:
**Chose:** `resolve_review` sets `effort` to `None` unless `[review] effort` is set (and also `None` when the provider has no effort levels). It does not fall back to `Provider::default_effort()`. For `provider = "none"`, `model` is `""` and `binary` is `None`.
**Over:** Falling back to the provider's default effort, as `Workers::resolved` does for workers.
**Because:** FR-2 calls review effort "optional", and leaving it unset passes no flag, so the CLI uses its own default. The worker rule (fall back to the provider's default) is spelled out only for `[workers]`.
**Undo:** Add `.or_else(|| p.default_effort().map(str::to_string))` in `review_from` (src/config.rs).

title: What does a collect do when no reviewer is chosen?
body:
**Chose:** with no reviewer chosen (no `[review] provider`, no legacy `agent`, no valid `FACTORY_REVIEW_PROVIDER`), `factory review collect` and the polish collect keep the legacy `[review]` defaults (Cursor, `cursor-agent`, `grok-4.7-high`) as before. Only `factory review second` prints `unreviewed: adversarial reviewer not set in config.toml — run factory setup review` and exits 2. The polish collect also re-reads `config.toml` at closeout, so a reviewer saved by answering the ask applies to the run that asked.
**Over:** making an unset reviewer `fallback owed — unreviewed: …` in collect too.
**Because:** the slice orders the unset message only for `review second`. A new run cannot reach closeout unset, because preflight asks first. Keeping the defaults leaves resumed runs and direct `review collect` calls as they were.
**Undo:** in `src/cli/review.rs` `collect_file` and `src/closeout.rs` `review_for`, replace the `ResolvedReview::from(&legacy)` fallback with an unreviewed result.

title: What does switching the review provider do to a legacy agent and the old model/effort?
body:
**Chose:** when `factory setup review` (wizard or `--provider`) switches the reviewer to another provider, it removes a legacy `[review] agent` whose binary belongs to a different CLI, and removes the old `model`/`effort` unless new ones are given, so the new provider's defaults apply.
**Over:** writing only `provider` and leaving `agent`, `model` and `effort` as they were.
**Because:** `resolve_review` passes `[review] agent` through as the binary to run for whatever provider is set, so a leftover `agent = "cursor-agent"` would run cursor-agent as the codex review, and a leftover `grok-…` model would go to codex. Model names and effort levels only make sense for one provider.
**Undo:** drop the `agent` unset and the `fresh` Keep→Clear mapping in `review_edits` (src/cli/setup.rs).

title: Does Enter on an unset provider prompt save the suggested CLI?
body:
**Chose:** on a provider prompt with no value saved yet (cockpit, review), the `[default]` shown is the first CLI found on PATH, and pressing Enter saves it. On every prompt that already has a saved value, and on every model/effort prompt, Enter writes nothing. An unset CI mode shows `[not set]`, and Enter leaves it unset.
**Over:** having Enter never write when nothing is saved yet.
**Because:** FR-3 says the provider prompt defaults "to current or first detected". Saving that default makes a full Enter-through run configure a reviewer, so slice 04's preflight ask goes away. CI has no default in PRD-025, so the wizard does not pick one.
**Undo:** map `Answer::Keep` to no edit in `cockpit_step`/`review_step` when `current` is `None`.
